nodes.body: On XPU this sends every `DeepEPMoE` through `quant_method.apply`, but only the unquantized path understands the DeepEP normal format. An FP8/MXFP4 checkpoint gets through startup and then crashes on the first forward (`'DeepEPNormalDispatchOutput' object has no attribute 'topk_output'`). Could we raise a clear `NotImplementedError` here for anything that isn't `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`?

This conflicts with #40671 on main, which already added `_deepep_import_error` and widened this to `except Exception`. When you rebase, please keep main's version and just import `deep_ep_xpu` inside it, otherwise this quietly reverts that fix for CUDA.

On XPU the loop only runs `x`, so this never fires and `best_dispatch_results` stays `None`. Line 313 then fails with `'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. Maybe `if isinstance(current_x, tuple) or DEVICE == "xpu":`? Did this run end to end on XPU?

This `.item()` is a host sync on every MoE layer every step (decode too, since XPU is forced to normal mode), and the trim doesn't save much: a lot of what `fused_experts` computes is still weight-0 padding. `num_recv_tokens_per_expert` is already on the host, so could you compact the valid slots with `torch.nonzero_static` instead, or have `prepare_moe_input` skip `-1`?

`group.size() <= 8` doesn't really mean intranode, e.g. 2 nodes x 4 GPUs passes. It also only fires once the buffer is built. An `nnodes > 1` check next to the other XPU checks in `handle_a2a_moe` would catch it at startup instead.

Where do users get `deep_ep_xpu`? It's not on PyPI and the PR doesn't link a repo. Could you put the install source and the minimum tested version in this message? The code relies on fairly specific APIs (`num_pcie_bytes`, `num_qps_per_rank`, `get_pcie_buffer_size_hint`).
Since this is disabled, CI never runs the XPU DeepEP path. Could you add a local GSM8K score and a throughput comparison against `--moe-a2a-backend none` to the PR description?

Nit: hooks here use `get_platform().is_xpu` (already imported) rather than `is_xpu()`, which also keeps it overridable in tests. That drops the new import too, which is the line that conflicts with main.

inline_comments.body: On XPU this sends every `DeepEPMoE` through `quant_method.apply`, but only the unquantized path understands the DeepEP normal format. An FP8/MXFP4 checkpoint gets through startup and then crashes on the first forward (`'DeepEPNormalDispatchOutput' object has no attribute 'topk_output'`). Could we raise a clear `NotImplementedError` here for anything that isn't `UnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`?

This conflicts with #40671 on main, which already added `_deepep_import_error` and widened this to `except Exception`. When you rebase, please keep main's version and just import `deep_ep_xpu` inside it, otherwise this quietly reverts that fix for CUDA.

On XPU the loop only runs `x`, so this never fires and `best_dispatch_results` stays `None`. Line 313 then fails with `'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. Maybe `if isinstance(current_x, tuple) or DEVICE == "xpu":`? Did this run end to end on XPU?

This `.item()` is a host sync on every MoE layer every step (decode too, since XPU is forced to normal mode), and the trim doesn't save much: a lot of what `fused_experts` computes is still weight-0 padding. `num_recv_tokens_per_expert` is already on the host, so could you compact the valid slots with `torch.nonzero_static` instead, or have `prepare_moe_input` skip `-1`?

`group.size() <= 8` doesn't really mean intranode, e.g. 2 nodes x 4 GPUs passes. It also only fires once the buffer is built. An `nnodes > 1` check next to the other XPU checks in `handle_a2a_moe` would catch it at startup instead.

Where do users get `deep_ep_xpu`? It's not on PyPI and the PR doesn't link a repo. Could you put the install source and the minimum tested version in this message? The code relies on fairly specific APIs (`num_pcie_bytes`, `num_qps_per_rank`, `get_pcie_buffer_size_hint`).
Since this is disabled, CI never runs the XPU DeepEP path. Could you add a local GSM8K score and a throughput comparison against `--moe-a2a-backend none` to the PR description?

Nit: hooks here use `get_platform().is_xpu` (already imported) rather than `is_xpu()`, which also keeps it overridable in tests. That drops the new import too, which is the line that conflicts with main.
